Today we celebrate Juneteenth, the day in 1865 when the last enslaved people in America finally learned they were free.

Juneteenth is a reminder of both how far this country has come and how much more we can do for everyone as a nation. The promise of freedom and equality for all Americans has never been fully realized, and the work of making it real continues.

In Congress, I continue to fight to make sure the people of California’s 19th Congressional District have access to the opportunities, rights, and protections that they deserve. That work is rooted in the belief that this country is strongest when every person has that opportunity.

Today, we honor the resilience and contributions of Black Americans who have fought for that freedom through generations of struggle and sacrifice. Their story is America’s story, and it deserves to be remembered not just today, but every day.

Let’s honor Juneteenth by recommitting ourselves to the work of building a more just and equal country for everyone..

Sincerely,
Jimmy

subject: SIX DAYS LATER, FLEMING STILL WON'T SAY WHETHER HE HAS RESIGNED FROM DC LOBBYING FIRM
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Julia Letlow for Louisiana
body:
New ethics law prohibits statewide elected officials from being paid by lobbying and consulting firms while serving in office

| | |
---
| | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ZGUiTCfGTTG?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a)
| | | | | | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEJune 19, 2026[katherine@julialetlow.com](mailto:katherine@julialetlow.com)
**SIX DAYS LATER, FLEMING STILL WON'T SAY WHETHER HE HAS RESIGNED FROM DC LOBBYING FIRM** _New ethics law prohibits statewide elected officials from being paid by lobbying and consulting firms while serving in office_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — Six days after Governor Jeff Landry signed House Bill 210 into law prohibiting statewide elected officials from being paid to lobby, advise, or consult while serving in office, State Treasurer John Fleming has yet to say whether he has resigned from the Washington lobbying firm that pays him or whether he intends to step down from office.
The law has immediate implications for Fleming, who joined The McKeon Group, a Washington lobbying and consulting firm, as a registered lobbyist in 2021 and remains listed as an advisor. During the Louisiana U.S. Senate debate, Fleming acknowledged that he receives monthly payments from the firm while simultaneously serving as Louisiana State Treasurer.
According to Fleming's financial disclosure forms, he received more than $40,000 from The McKeon Group in 2024 while also collecting a taxpayer-funded salary from the State of Louisiana.
Despite the law taking effect nearly a week ago, Fleming has not publicly announced whether he has severed ties with the firm or how he intends to comply with the new ethics requirements.
_"Six days have passed, and John Fleming still hasn't given the people of Louisiana an answer,"_**said Congresswoman Julia Letlow.**_"The law is clear. Statewide elected officials cannot be paid by lobbying and consulting firms while serving in office. If John Fleming wants to remain State Treasurer, he should resign from the McKeon Group. If he wants to remain on the payroll of a Washington lobbying firm, he should resign as State Treasurer."_
Governor Landry and the Legislature acted to strengthen Louisiana's ethics laws and prohibit arrangements that allow statewide elected officials to simultaneously serve in public office while being paid by lobbying and consulting firms.
To date, Fleming has not publicly stated which path he intends to take.

body:
Plus: Only 29% of Democrats are still proud to be American. | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/16zmDoilmuU?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | | At two New Mexico smoke shops, most of what's on the shelves isn't food.
Somehow, they're now among the biggest SNAP retailers in the state. And the state is about to find out who's paying for it.
[Then Harry Enten put a number on national pride this week.](https://us.list-manage.com/19kP55ZdHiv?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e) The Democratic side of the chart is unrecognizable.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/81B1giyXLve?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | 🔥 **SNAP FRAUD: TWO NM SMOKE SHOPS RAKED IN $878K**
One pulled in $435,999. The other pulled in $442,539. About seven times what an average convenience store sees in a year. Their own online profiles include 81 photos of inventory. Want to guess how many showed something a SNAP card can legally buy?
Two. Water and soda.
**Sen. Pat Woods just sent USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins a letter that names names and lays out the timeline. We walk through the receipts.

** 🇺🇸 **ONLY 29% OF DEMOCRATS ARE PROUD TO BE AMERICAN**
In 2001, the number was 85%. Today it's 29%. That's a collapse.
Harry Enten laid out the data on displaying the American flag, what July 4th means, and national pride.
Mark shares what a friend learned in a UNM classroom recently when he asked one simple question about the American system. Not one student would concede the point. This is what the next generation is being taught. And we go there.
---
| [Stream No Doubt About It Podcast Now](https://us.list-manage.com/E8c1_u9cQU1?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | 🏔️ **MAYOR BJ LINDSAY ON THE BUILDER WHO'S DONE WITH NEW MEXICO**
Angel Fire Mayor BJ Lindsay joined us this week — and he didn't pull punches.
Abrazo Homes co-founder Mackenzie Bishop just told the Albuquerque Journal that launching operations in Texas is a "near weekly temptation." The permit numbers explain why. Texas issued 16,572 building permits in April. New Mexico issued 583. Lubbock County outbuilt Bernalillo with half the population.
BJ's been a general contractor in NM long enough to know exactly why this is happening — and what Angel Fire just pulled off with workforce housing that proves it doesn't have to.
Plus a Mark vs the Mountain episode 5 reveal you'll want to see.

| **U.S. to Intervene in Judicial Watch’s Reparations Lawsuit****[](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83597&L=38075&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1XS0pfUVZtcFUtMCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3287cc24ac2219c56ae972d6ab08892aba5c452f9c501ff9431bc7c5d7d3b95b)**The U.S. Department of Justice has filed a[motion to intervene](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83597&L=38054&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2ZsaW5uLWV0LWFsLXYtY2l0eS1vZi1ldmFuc3Rvbi11c2EtaW50ZXJ2ZW50aW9uLTA0MjY5Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=55ef0c15862baa713d4ae311bf573cdc7652b3f7a92a193fa5ede10e776e6f95) in our class action civil rights lawsuit challenging the City of Evanston’s reparations program, which makes $25,000 direct cash payments to black residents and descendants of black residents who lived in Evanston, Illinois, between 1919 and 1969.The United States filed its motion and a proposed complaint in intervention in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois in our May 2024 [lawsuit](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83597&L=32489&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvcmVwYXJhdGlvbnMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=e2f17164aa218b80367569984ffc689ca37a00bd814f1152d75d97e5366734ad) ([_Flinn et al. v. City of Evanston_](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83597&L=32473&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2ZsaW5uLXYtZXZhbnN0b24tcmVwYXJhdGlvbi1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDQyNjkvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=ef1226e71ba572063d1d869b1a65efa1ea5da643866093e9278f934964277209) (No. 1:24-cv-04269)). We are assisted by Christine Svenson of Svenson Legal, LLC.The Justice Department’s proposed complaint in intervention names the City of Evanston as a defendant and alleges that the program violates the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment. The Justice Department also alleges the program violates the Fair Housing Act.The United States asserts that it has an unconditional right to intervene under Section 902 of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, 42 U.S.C. § 2000h-2, which allows the attorney general to intervene in cases alleging the denial of equal protection of the laws on account of race when the case is certified to be of general public importance. body:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133656956/628661050/1231236074?refcode=RS_EM_EN_2026.06.19_Juneteenth&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NzI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiODQ5YmU5Ni01MjZjLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xd4VkE93b9GWMux3IuRrABhWoZDcslsdVrl9OV8kPok=&emci=51813aa2-386c-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b6d6&emdi=b849be96-526c-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b6d6&ceid=23483442) | Hi Peter, Walking through our local Juneteenth celebration today, I reflected on two truths. 1) Our country was built on so much hatred and violence and cruelty — no matter how much this Administration tries to erase the truth. 2) The story of Black America is also one of joy and resiliency and love and community. **Today marks 160 years since the news of emancipation reached enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, finally ending chattel slavery in the United States.** From that day on, lawmakers have tried time and time again to develop systems that disenfranchise and dehumanize Black Americans. To gut the Voting Rights Act, to deny military officer commendations, to strip funding from Black Maternal Health programs, and to attack our safety net. And with every vile, racist attempt, it is people — coming together in community and solidarity — that keep us moving forward. **This Juneteenth, I celebrate that history of resilience and commit to continuing to work arm in arm with Black activists, civic leaders, and neighbors who seek to redress past and present sins of this country in pursuit of a more just America.** ❤️💚🖤 — Emily | | Emily Randall is proud to represent Washington’s 6th District in Congress. She grew up in a working-class Union household in Port Orchard and was the first in her family to attend college. clean_body: | Hi Peter, Walking through our local Juneteenth celebration today, I reflected on two truths. 1) Our country was built on so much hatred and violence and cruelty — no matter how much this Administration tries to erase the truth. 2) The story of Black America is also one of joy and resiliency and love and community. Today marks 160 years since the news of emancipation reached enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, finally ending chattel slavery in the United States. From that day on, lawmakers have tried time and time again to develop systems that disenfranchise and dehumanize Black Americans. To gut the Voting Rights Act, to deny military officer commendations, to strip funding from Black Maternal Health programs, and to attack our safety net. And with every vile, racist attempt, it is people — coming together in community and solidarity — that keep us moving forward. This Juneteenth, I celebrate that history of resilience and commit to continuing to work arm in arm with Black activists, civic leaders, and neighbors who seek to redress past and present sins of this country in pursuit of a more just America. ❤️💚🖤 — Emily | | Emily Randall is proud to represent Washington’s 6th District in Congress. | | Dear Peter,

Today is Juneteenth, the day we celebrate the end of the Civil War and the smashing of slavery, one of the most brutally oppressive systems the world has ever known. American capitalism was built on the exploitation of enslaved Black people and the genocide of indigenous peoples. The horrors of slavery, Jim Crow segregation, and the ongoing exploitation of Black working people have provided unimaginable wealth for a tiny elite, while impoverishing generations of Black Americans and their communities.
The end of slavery was not won by the voices of “moderation,” who at the time argued for a kinder, gentler form of slavery and for a process of gradual change, and who derided abolitionists as divisive and uncouth people. This victory did not belong to those who attached themselves to the two parties of American capitalism, at that time the Whig Party and the Democratic Party, both of which defended the system of slavery. It did not belong to the Uncle Toms of the day. Instead, it belonged to the Black, brown and white troops who courageously fought and defeated the slave-owning class on the battlefields. And yes, it was a multi-racial struggle that succeeded in crushing the white slaveholders.
While slavery was defeated, the horrors of institutional racism were not. That is why our antiwar pro-worker Congressional campaign is fighting against racism and all oppression.
**Neither of the Democrats running in this race, Adam Smith and Melissa Chaudhry, even mention the needs of the Black community on their campaign websites.** Kshama is the only candidate in this race fighting for Black working-class and poor people and the only candidate with the track record of winning victories for the Black community.
Kshama is fighting for reparations for Black working-class and poor people, funded by taxing the rich. The net worth of the top one percent of the United States is at a shocking [$55 trillion](https://us.list-manage.com/cW6Arh20zLG?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15). We need to tax the rich to fund massive investment in Black and historically Black communities. We need quality affordable housing in Black communities, and strong national rent control. We need free public college and university, including a major increase in funding for Historically Black Colleges & Universities (HBCUs) and an expansion of community colleges in Black neighborhoods. We need to build free public healthcare clinics in every Black community as part of a free national healthcare system. We need to expand mass transit and make it free, including by ensuring high-quality, frequent, accessible public transit routes in every Black community.
Kshama is fighting for a public-sector living-wage jobs guarantee funded by taxing the rich. As part of this, Kshama is also calling for a national program to create hundreds of thousands of jobs for Black workers to help carry out the critical work of rebuilding infrastructure, expanding mass transit, and transforming our energy system.
We need to end mass incarceration, ban for-profit prisons, and stop forced, unpaid, and low-wage prison labor. We need to bring an end to racist policing and put police departments under the control of democratically elected community boards with full power over department policy, hiring, and firing. We need to put an end to the disastrous “war on drugs,” and instead fund healthcare, housing, education, and support for small businesses alongside a major expansion of living-wage union jobs.
Democratic Congressmember Adam Smith, who is Kshama’s main opponent, has had a long record of slashing hundreds of billions of dollars from Medicare, Medicaid, social services, and public housing. He was also one of the many Democrats who voted for the bailouts of the billionaires in the wake of the 2008 Great Recession. The bailout policies plundered the millions of working people who faced home foreclosures and handed over tens of billions of dollars worth of real estate to private equity. This bipartisan robbery against working people is a big reason why rents have been skyrocketing. All of these policies voted for by Adam Smith have disproportionately and severely undermined the living standards of Black working-class and poor people.
As the only socialist on Seattle’s City Council, Kshama Sawant led the fight to win the Amazon Tax, which funds hundreds of millions of dollars of affordable housing every year by taxing big corporations like Amazon. Kshama also campaigned for housing justice for Black working and poor people alongside “an expansive coalition of nonprofit organizations, faith-based institutions, and affordable housing providers,” including hosting a [major rally](https://us.list-manage.com/15aS0LZd9lW?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) for “reparations, unity, and affordable housing” in the summer of 2021. Kshama’s office used that public momentum to dedicate [millions of dollars](https://us.list-manage.com/Xw85RgDEFCz?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) of the Amazon Tax she won in 2020 specifically towards building [housing for the Black community](https://us.list-manage.com/ZT6RLeK0IAU?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) in Seattle’s historically Black Central District, a form of reparations. She also helped win $500,000 to fund the [Garfield Super Block and community center](https://us.list-manage.com/Zx0vFmEQMM7?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) in the Central District. She helped organize Black and other marginalized-community tenants at [Chateau Apartments](https://us.list-manage.com/JfRMScM7Yy3?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) and [Rainier Court](https://us.list-manage.com/19q7U_2o6JO?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) to successfully fight and win against the mass evictions and rent increases attempted by their exploitative landlords. We need to organize millions of people around the country and build a movement to win these kinds of victories on a much larger scale. Through her annual People’s Budget campaign, Kshama won full public funding for [legal defense](https://us.list-manage.com/hpLGAWlJZzB?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) for any working-class renters facing eviction. Statistical evidence indicates that Black community members, particularly women, disproportionately face evictions and that trained legal counsel dramatically increases the likelihood of preventing evictions.
The greatest material improvement in the lives of Black American workers came through the mass labor movements of the 1930s and 1940s and the creation of the Congress of Industrial Organizations, which built fighting multiracial unions and helped to power the Civil Rights movement. We need to rebuild a fighting, anti-racist labor movement.
In solidarity,Kshama for Congress

clean_body: End the War on Black People! | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Kshama Sawant is the ONLY candidate in WA's 9th Congressional District race who has beaten the billionaires. Kshama is also the ONLY candidate in the race fighting to win free healthcare for all funded by taxing the rich , to end all military aid to Israel , to stop the AI data centers and mass layoffs , and for a public-sector living-wage jobs guarantee. | | | JOIN US FOR OUR JUNE VOLUNTEER DAY THIS SATURDAY, JUNE 20th AT 11:00AM Judkins Park Light Rail Station, SeattleOthello Light Rail Station, SeattleFederal Way Farmers Market | | | Not in Seattle, or can't make it to Volunteer Day? or sign up for another sign up for another ! | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Dear Peter, Today is Juneteenth, the day we celebrate the end of the Civil War and the smashing of slavery, one of the most brutally oppressive systems the world has ever known. American capitalism was built on the exploitation of enslaved Black people and the genocide of indigenous peoples. The horrors of slavery, Jim Crow segregation, and the ongoing exploitation of Black working people have provided unimaginable wealth for a tiny elite, while impoverishing generations of Black Americans and their communities. The end of slavery was not won by the voices of “moderation,” who at the time argued for a kinder, gentler form of slavery and for a process of gradual change, and who derided abolitionists as divisive and uncouth people. This victory did not belong to those who attached themselves to the two parties of American capitalism, at that time the Whig Party and the Democratic Party, both of which defended the system of slavery. It did not belong to the Uncle Toms of the day. Instead, it belonged to the Black, brown and white troops who courageously fought and defeated the slave-owning class on the battlefields. And yes, it was a multi-racial struggle that succeeded in crushing the white slaveholders. While slavery was defeated, the horrors of institutional racism were not. That is why our antiwar pro-worker Congressional campaign is fighting against racism and all oppression. Neither of the Democrats running in this race, Adam Smith and Melissa Chaudhry, even mention the needs of the Black community on their campaign websites. Kshama is the only candidate in this race fighting for Black working-class and poor people and the only candidate with the track record of winning victories for the Black community. Kshama is fighting for reparations for Black working-class and poor people, funded by taxing the rich. The net worth of the top one percent of the United States is at a shocking . We need to tax the rich to fund massive investment in Black and historically Black communities. We need quality affordable housing in Black communities, and strong national rent control. We need free public college and university, including a major increase in funding for Historically Black Colleges & Universities (HBCUs) and an expansion of community colleges in Black neighborhoods. We need to build free public healthcare clinics in every Black community as part of a free national healthcare system. We need to expand mass transit and make it free, including by ensuring high-quality, frequent, accessible public transit routes in every Black community. Kshama is fighting for a public-sector living-wage jobs guarantee funded by taxing the rich. As part of this, Kshama is also calling for a national program to create hundreds of thousands of jobs for Black workers to help carry out the critical work of rebuilding infrastructure, expanding mass transit, and transforming our energy system. We need to end mass incarceration, ban for-profit prisons, and stop forced, unpaid, and low-wage prison labor. We need to bring an end to racist policing and put police departments under the control of democratically elected community boards with full power over department policy, hiring, and firing. We need to put an end to the disastrous “war on drugs,” and instead fund healthcare, housing, education, and support for small businesses alongside a major expansion of living-wage union jobs. Democratic Congressmember Adam Smith, who is Kshama’s main opponent, has had a long record of slashing hundreds of billions of dollars from Medicare, Medicaid, social services, and public housing. He was also one of the many Democrats who voted for the bailouts of the billionaires in the wake of the 2008 Great Recession. The bailout policies plundered the millions of working people who faced home foreclosures and handed over tens of billions of dollars worth of real estate to private equity. This bipartisan robbery against working people is a big reason why rents have been skyrocketing. All of these policies voted for by Adam Smith have disproportionately and severely undermined the living standards of Black working-class and poor people. As the only socialist on Seattle’s City Council, Kshama Sawant led the fight to win the Amazon Tax, which funds hundreds of millions of dollars of affordable housing every year by taxing big corporations like Amazon. Kshama also campaigned for housing justice for Black working and poor people alongside “an expansive coalition of nonprofit organizations, faith-based institutions, and affordable housing providers,” including hosting a for “reparations, unity, and affordable housing” in the summer of 2021. Kshama’s office used that public momentum to dedicate of the Amazon Tax she won in 2020 specifically towards building in Seattle’s historically Black Central District, a form of reparations. She also helped win $500,000 to fund the in the Central District. She helped organize Black and other marginalized-community tenants at and to successfully fight and win against the mass evictions and rent increases attempted by their exploitative landlords. We need to organize millions of people around the country and build a movement to win these kinds of victories on a much larger scale. Through her annual People’s Budget campaign, Kshama won full public funding for for any working-class renters facing eviction. Statistical evidence indicates that Black community members, particularly women, disproportionately face evictions and that trained legal counsel dramatically increases the likelihood of preventing evictions. The greatest material improvement in the lives of Black American workers came through the mass labor movements of the 1930s and 1940s and the creation of the Congress of Industrial Organizations, which built fighting multiracial unions and helped to power the Civil Rights movement. We need to rebuild a fighting, anti-racist labor movement. The Republican Party of Green County joined with Dane and Rock Counties for a stellar tri-county Pints and Politics night on Tuesday, June 2. Attendees heard from an array of first-class guest speakers. Members also attended a Memorial Day Service at the Brooklyn Area Veterans Memorial, hosted by Chairman John Fandrich. **Green Lake County**
Attendees at the annual June Dairy Days Parade in Markesan on Saturday, June 13th saw Republicans of Green Lake walking with their classic Elephant Float! **Monroe County**
Monroe County Republicans were out in force on June 6th at the Monroe County Dairy Breakfast, showing strong support for their local and state-wide candidates and standing with the farmers who keep communities thriving. It was a great morning at the Trescher Farm in Cashton, celebrating agriculture, neighbors, and the values that make Monroe County strong.

The Sparta Butterfest parade had a number of attendees, including Rep. Nancy VanderMeer, Secretary of State candidate Nate Pollnow, Sheriff Wes Revels, and Sheriff candidate Chris Weaver. **Sauk County**
Republicans of Sauk County sponsored and hosted a joint Flag Day / Trump Birthday Party this past Sunday, the 14th. The party was a hit. **St. Croix County**
Republicans of St. Croix absolutely jam-packed their last two weeks, putting in incredible work for conservatism in the county. Several members attended the Trump Roundtable in Chippewa Falls, and other members packed up to represent at back-to-back parades, the Somerset Pea Soup Day Parade and the Baldwin Windmill Days Parade. Rob Kreibich for Assembly came in for reinforcement during the Windmill Days Parade. To finish it all off, St. Croix County Republicans participated in a flag wave for President Trump's birthday and Flag Day. **Pepin County**
Pepin County showed up for our country this past Flag Day: 30 of their members volunteered their Sunday to wave flags and celebrate birthdays (America's 250th and President Trump's 80th). The patriots were met with cheers and honks from drivers passing by. The Department of Justice has now joined MAGA's desperate fight to save the GOP Senate and House majorities from annihilation in the upcoming 2026 Midterm elections.
In a recently unveiled lawsuit the DOJ will now attempt to axe the National Voter Registration Act which prevents states from purging their voter registration rolls in the 90 days prior to an election.

If their suit is successful red states would be able to cull their voter files of millions of Democratic voters the day before the election thereby ensuring these voters have no way to update their registration or challenge their erroneous removal from the registration file.
In a 2024 shadow docket ruling (the U.S. Supreme Court's emergency non-merits docket, used for expedited immediate relief) they ruled this practice was constitutional though the ruling only applied to a unique scenario in Virginia.
But now the Court appears ready to make this the law of the land.
When they do this, there will be nothing standing in the way of every Republican Governor in America purging their registered voters list on Monday, November 2nd, the day before the election and removing every registered Democratic voter from their rolls.
These voters will show up at the polls ready to vote only to be turned away and told too bad, so sad as it will no longer be possible to reregister. If they challenge their removal, the appeal decision will only come long after the election has passed.
In competitive red states like North Carolina, Nebraska, Georgia, and Louisiana (yes, even Louisiana is in the cards for Dems this year) this will ensure that Democrats do not win the critical Senate and House seats that are required for reclaiming Dem majorities in the House and Senate.
So what can we do?
The answer is two fold, ensure Dems hold as many state supreme courts as possible, our first line of defense to stop aggressive purge efforts. And second, ensure that the moment Democrats reclaim control in DC that we take immediate action to eliminate the Supreme Court's conservative majority by any means necessary including by packing the court.

However, if the Supreme Court rules in favor of DOJ even this won’t | | | | | == | Peter, The Department of Justice has now joined MAGA's desperate fight to save the GOP Senate and House majorities from annihilation in the upcoming 2026 Midterm elections. In a recently unveiled lawsuit the DOJ will now attempt to axe the National Voter Registration Act which prevents states from purging their voter registration rolls in the 90 days prior to an election. | == If their suit is successful red states would be able to cull their voter files of millions of Democratic voters the day before the election thereby ensuring these voters have no way to update their registration or challenge their erroneous removal from the registration file. In a 2024 shadow docket ruling (the U.S. Supreme Court's emergency non-merits docket, used for expedited immediate relief) they ruled this practice was constitutional though the ruling only applied to a unique scenario in Virginia. But now the Court appears ready to make this the law of the land. When they do this, there will be nothing standing in the way of every Republican Governor in America purging their registered voters list on Monday, November 2nd, the day before the election and removing every registered Democratic voter from their rolls. These voters will show up at the polls ready to vote only to be turned away and told too bad, so sad as it will no longer be possible to reregister. If they challenge their removal, the appeal decision will only come long after the election has passed. In competitive red states like North Carolina, Nebraska, Georgia, and Louisiana (yes, even Louisiana is in the cards for Dems this year) this will ensure that Democrats do not win the critical Senate and House seats that are required for reclaiming Dem majorities in the House and Senate. So what can we do? The answer is two fold, ensure Dems hold as many state supreme courts as possible, our first line of defense to stop aggressive purge efforts. And second, ensure that the moment Democrats reclaim control in DC that we take immediate action to eliminate the Supreme Court's conservative majority by any means necessary including by packing the court. Defend our Courts performs both of these functions. We defend Democratic state supreme court majorities and go after conservative ones AND we are building the movement to reclaim the Supreme Court of the United States. Peter,

The primaries are over. The two parties have chosen their nominees. **Now the people of Maine have a choice to make.** Do we want more partisan politics, more division, and more excuses? Or do we want a Governor who answers only to the people of Maine? That’s why I’m running as an independent.

Meanwhile, for too many Maine families, the basics keep getting further out of reach, a home you can afford, health care within reach, child care you can count on, lower energy bills, and a good job that lets you build a life here in Maine. **I do not answer to party bosses. I answer only to you.** As Governor, I’ll be relentlessly focused on results: making life more affordable, growing Maine’s economy, and restoring trust in government – because I have always done what is best for the people of Maine, regardless of the political fallout. Today is the first day of the general election campaign. If you believe Maine deserves a Governor who answers only to its people, not political insiders, now is the time to step in.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | Jacob Davis's Market Brief (ads) | | • | Behind the Markets ---|--- | • | Weiss Ratings Plus ---|--- | • | Salem Media Group ---|--- | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. ## Truce in Lebanon as Talks Stall
A U.S.-backed [ceasefire took effect](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQBuCngc3IHOCEwUMXtnTtiM72kTi92Mg2oenTV-QVOp5O-vV__9dlvqBnH66f-CBdljgH2jNTKZRmnzDcKa6YnP-lXJC_cy6boxkkKCGVADk79Pya-9rphQioq0m3p3M7DrJVfX3TbugMyU6NEi2dR6ST7ReyqhvQDdZA7fWRJhXIVsoRoDG4GAIYBmWMoXNf9ZKcLzE19-hDudHCr_ik1Nj4qFnfSllz1X1UMFUw7fveLPHnUBz_Cib2TxLHXcG0ZXGgxEpoSThCFmGzTJjEWyfWmMsaAznhc0JiwWQwxCBsDAt7W8R9CyTasU7arbtn9lmdql5eH-j53aj8a8anhr8AAAD__2goixM) between Israel and Hezbollah on Friday afternoon, hours after Israeli forces struck more than 80 targets in southern Lebanon, where four Israeli soldiers and at least 18 civilians were killed. ## Final State Report Details Camp Mystic Failures
State investigators delivered their [final report on the Camp Mystic disaster](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAMQE8TuiDHsJmlSLEN3d92S2SI-RNNICixhuH2q8wc4TduLPn5vX9f0xeFGPbvv7Sxk9eapp3PElmE87SGneJC27FdRcKS-UhZipBMCGg1WI0weQrxmvrGuxn8YBp25vbbDL-6rsfm7iyvlolmhn6w0HNngZgQjJ09A89NcPUYWARjAM3QDrAM3KGx1M233ljVA_sgKbdyZ-EXlTVe6cm5XdLWRHcXOYrq_igcFY7nebaPQlKXCsdqo3CMaaGocKwohSPUYQaFo9CD6aSr6DWnTVc51pHOjR6ci34X0B9xHXZJ2jP5eOlaRX-y6DWm5Culyc4fZ4gxFHtTPXxvFOL7S_lZ26fD_wEAAP__oHKPcQ) Thursday, finding that a missing emergency plan and stalled evacuation contributed to the deaths of 25 campers and two counselors in last July's flood. Investigators Casey Garrett and Michael Massengale, hired by the Legislature, described cascading failures: despite storm alerts and a 1:14 a.m. flash flood warning, no one moved campers to higher ground. Peter: It’s Alex Vindman, humbly asking you to donate just $3 to my Senate campaign in Florida. I am running to unseat one of Donald Trump’s most loyal allies — Republican Ashley Moody — and it would mean the world to have your support before my FEC deadline.

While you probably didn’t wake up this morning thinking you would donate to flip Florida’s Senate seat, that is what I am asking you to do. Let me explain.
This is an unprecedented moment for our nation. The corruption we’re seeing from Washington is staggering: Donald Trump and his billionaires are robbing this country blind — and Senator Ashley Moody is doing everything possible to support it.
America needs a leader who has a track record of taking on tough fights and can turn our country around in this critical moment. That is why I am asking:
$3 to help reach undecided Florida voters, before Donald Trump’s allies do.
$3 to stand up against the attacks from the billionaires and special interest groups, who will spend whatever it takes to protect Ashley Moody.
$3 to help take back the Senate and restore law and order.
[**Can you pitch in $3 (or more, if you can afford it) before our FEC fundraising deadline? | |
Consequences of Democrat’s Radical Immigration Policies
.As the court case proceeds for Jose Medina, the man charged with the tragic murder of 18-year-old Loyola University freshman Sheridan Gorman, the reality of this heartbreaking situation continues to unfold. Medina was back in court recently for a status hearing and has pleaded not guilty to all charges, which include first-degree murder and attempted first-degree murder. Sheridan's family attended the hearing, where they shared a powerful statement **calling for immediate changes to our nation's immigration policies.**
.As reported by CBS News, **Medina is a Venezuelan migrant who was living in the U.S. illegally** , a fact confirmed by the Department of Homeland Security.
This devastating loss highlights exactly why we must take immediate action. The influx of millions of illegals under the previous administration is draining our resources and making our communities less safe, putting us all at risk. While Niki Conforti fully supports legal immigration, she firmly believes that the previous administration’s open-border policies were unacceptable. In Congress, Niki plans to prevent future tragedies like this by **fighting for strict immigration reforms** and prioritizing public safety:

1. 1\. Securing the Border: The federal government must enforce the laws on the southern border and continue constructing the wall.
2. 2\. Deporting Violent Criminals: Niki supports expanding ICE and ensuring the swift deportation of violent criminals.

While **Democrats like Sean Casten support dangerous policies that shield violent criminals** from deportation, we know the truth: refusing to deport these offenders makes every resident of the 6th District less safe. We must prioritize the safety of our communities and enforce the law to protect our citizens. Please keep Sheridan Gorman’s family in your prayers as they seek justice.
Stay informed on this issue—[**read the full breakdown here**](https://us.list-manage.com/19mNMcYtM_A?e=25f4fa3311&c2id=7b058fb5598c3e136d157ed790328086)**.**

We warmly invite you to participate and walk alongside Niki Conforti and our campaign team to celebrate the 250th anniversary of America at the **Annual Independence Day Parade in Villa Park.**
* **Date:** Saturday, July 4, 2026.
* **Time:** Staging takes place from 8:30 AM to 9:30 AM, steps off at 10:00 AM.
* **Location:** Route begins at Park Blvd. and Summit Ave. in Villa Park.
* **Theme:** "Stars, Stripes, and 250 Lights," hosted by the Villa Park VFW Post 2801.

Celebrate and walk alongside Niki Conforti and our campaign team at the **Village of Downers Grove Independence Day Parade**!
* **Date:** Saturday, July 4, 2026.
* **Time:** Parade steps off at 1:00 p.m.
* **Location/Route:** Steps off from Main St. and Grant St. and travels south on Main St. to Warren Ave. in Downtown Downers Grove.

We’re organizing voters to speak out against this power grab. name: Douglas Carswell
subject: The Federal Scholarship Tax Credit – What You Need to Know
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/mississippiwins-12853696?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
Let me introduce you to three letters you are going to hear a great deal about in the months ahead: SGO.

If they mean nothing to you today, they soon will. SGO stands for Scholarship Granting Organization — and thanks to a change in federal law, Mississippi is about to see a whole network of them spring up, channeling tens of millions of dollars into Mississippi schools.

This is about to become a big deal. Here is how it works.

Every year, you — like millions of Mississippi taxpayers — send a chunk of your income to the IRS.

Thanks to the new federal tax credit, you can chose to redirect $1,700 of it to a local SGO, rather than give it to Washington. You get to decide where that slice of your own tax dollars go.

The SGO then uses the money you give it to fund places at local schools.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/ZaxNHJdCIJ3?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)
---
_Everything you need to know about the Tax Credit and SGOs_
| Yesterday I sat and listened to the inspirational T. Mac Howard, Founder and Head of School for Delta Streets Academy in Greenwood talking about the work his team is doing to extend education opportunities in the Delta. As I did so, I was struck by a simple thought: would you rather give $1,700 of your tax dollars to the federal government, or give it to provide a classical or Christian education to young people in our state?

This ought not to be a hard sell.

Mississippi is well placed to seize it. It's not just Delta Streets, but Redeemer's, Vineyard — in fact, we have dozens of other non-government schools spread across our state.

I think we are about to see a flurry of activity to set up SGOs – and rightly so. And it will be the Governor, Tate Reeves, who decides which organizations that apply to become SGOs get designation. Choosing a strong slate of SGOs could prove to be one of the most consequential decisions of Gov Reeves' entire time in office, if it helps lay the foundations for change.

Here at MCPP, our job is to make sure Mississippians understand this opportunity — and seize it. So at our education freedom website, [CompareMySchool.com](https://us.list-manage.com/10Ee3AZKQz4?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3), we have a plain-English guide to the tax credit - and a fact sheet you can download, print, and share.
---
|
---
| We will even host the definitive **Mississippi SGO Index** : a register of every approved local SGO, rated against key metrics, so taxpayers can act with confidence and parents can see their options at a glance.

This is a rare opportunity. Let us make the most of it.
---
| [Forward this email to a friend!](https://us.list-manage.com/iCxyOI7JtIi?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3 "Forward this email to a friend!")
---
| |
---
Warm regards,

Douglas Carswell
President & CEO
Mississippi Center for Public Policy

disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Dave Beckwith For Congress_
body:
| | | | [](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
---
| | Dear Friend,
Last month, Governor Abigail Spanberger signed one of the most sweeping attacks on Second Amendment rights in Virginia's history. Starting July 1st, it will be illegal in the Commonwealth of Virginia to buy, sell, manufacture, transfer, or import semiautomatic rifles, pistols, and shotguns that can hold more than 15 rounds of ammunition.
Before I get into what happened in Richmond, I want to share some exciting news. This week, with over 179 people in attendance, **our campaign won the VA-10 Republican primary debate straw poll with an 89.7% majority**. I am grateful for every person who stood with us, and I want to keep that momentum going.
---
| | |
---
**If you have been thinking about contributing to this race,_today is the day._**
[DONATE TO DAVE](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
|
---
| | | Now, back to what happened in Richmond.
In plain terms, the AR-15, one of the most commonly owned firearms in America, is now effectively banned from future sale in Virginia. Law-abiding gun owners who already own these firearms can keep them. But if you want to purchase one after July 1st, the state of Virginia says you cannot.
I swore an oath to defend the Constitution 30 years ago. That oath did not expire when I retired. The Second Amendment is a fundamental right, not a privilege granted by government, and what Governor Spanberger signed is a direct assault on that right. The NRA and Gun Owners of America have already filed lawsuits and I believe the courts will strike this down. But the fact that it passed at all is a warning about what happens when one party controls everything in Richmond with no checks and no balance. Let's make sure this doesn't happen in Congress

God Bless, Dave Beckwith

subject: ICYMI: Another important announcement from me >>

body:
I’m doubling down on my support

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2934%2E4032634%2EsUS2nn)
---
ICYMI — I wanted to make sure you saw this important update on what our grassroots movement is making possible. Earlier this year, I announced that I contributed over $400,000 from my campaign account to 23 state parties to ensure Democrats win up and down the ballot in November. **I wanted to reach out and share an update: Our team recently raised an additional $400,000 to give to state parties in North Carolina, Ohio, Michigan, Maine, Georgia, and Alaska.** [**I’ll share more on my decision below, and if you’re able to pitch in $28 or anything you can to support our campaign, you’ll ensure we can continue investing in taking back our majorities this November.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3677?amount=28&t=8&akid=2934%2E4032634%2EsUS2nn) These six states have some of the most competitive Senate races of the cycle — and I think Democrats can win if we have the resources we need to put up a fight. We need to gain four seats to take back the Senate, which means we need to put up a strong defense in Michigan and Georgia, AND a strong offense in Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, and Alaska. This money is how we fight back — hiring organizers, airing ads, and reaching out to more voters. Because Democrats can’t just talk the talk about the midterm elections being critical. We have to put our money where our mouth is. Republicans certainly are. Billionaire donors and giant corporations are giving them buckets of money they can use to cling onto their power in the midterms. That’s why I’m doubling down on my support for these state parties. **This team has now helped contribute over $800,000 dollars to state parties across the country. Because this is what it takes to stop Trump’s corruption and get our government to work for working people.** [**If you can, please pitch in $28 or whatever you can to support projects like this one. And let’s win big.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3677?amount=28&t=9&akid=2934%2E4032634%2EsUS2nn)

Friend,

I want to start by saying thank you so much for supporting my campaign for governor.

I know you've been receiving a lot of emails from my team and from me asking for your donation, but we wouldn't be reaching out so much if it weren't absolutely critical.
You see, New Mexico is a top pickup opportunity for the GOP, and all eyes are on our race — **especially because they know governors are the first line of defense when the federal government abuses its power as it has been.** New Mexicans are already feeling the effects of Donald Trump’s cuts to Medicaid and SNAP, the firing of federal workers, and rising costs for working families. That’s why having a governor who is ready on day one matters. I’ve led a 70,000-person workforce, managed an $18 billion budget, and had five bills signed into law by Donald Trump. I’ve also gone up against him before — and won. I am ready to focus on and fight for New Mexicans from day one. We will lower costs, strengthen our schools, protect our communities, and ensure every New Mexican has the opportunity to get ahead.
**With so much on the line, I need to know I can count on you to help show the GOP we have what it takes to win and keep New Mexico blue:_[Please, will you chip in $5 or more now to help me reach my $10,000 goal before midnight tonight?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12039?refcode=jtk892-fr-nd&t=2&akid=10385%2E400544%2ER_25y6)_**

name: Chris Pappas
subject: The reality of a tied race (And what we do next)
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=7301%2E582294%2EWa3rBm ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=7301%2E582294%2EWa3rBm ]Chris Pappas for Senate

I need to be direct with you: Recent polling shows our
lead is slipping.

[ TIED ]TIED New Hampshire Senate Race: Sununu: 44%, Pappas: 45%

National Republicans are pouring in cash and surging to try to flip this
seat, and it’s working.

This is a reminder of how close this race really is – and how quickly
momentum can shift when outside spending ramps up.

The path to the Senate runs through New Hampshire, and the GOP knows it.

If Democrats are going to have any chance of taking back the majority, we
have to match their energy right now to organize, communicate, and ensure
we’re reaching every single voter between now and Election Day.

If you’re looking for the right moment to join this grassroots movement,
this is it. We are counting on your support to fight back against the GOP
and gather the resources we need to be successful in November. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260620_1.PjuRLh&refcode=em20260620-1&t=1003&akid=7301%2E582294%2EWa3rBm ]Will you
chip in $5 today?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260620_1.PjuRLh&amount=5&refcode=em20260620-1&t=1022&akid=7301%2E582294%2EWa3rBm ]Donate $5 »

John Sununu has made it clear he’ll stand with Donald Trump and protect
his agenda in the Senate. And right now, we’re tied.

If Republicans win here in New Hampshire, it will cement a MAGA Senate
majority for years to come – and give Trump unchecked power in Washington.

I’ve taken on tough fights before, and I know we can win this one, too.
But only if we have the resources to fight back immediately. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260620_1.PjuRLh&refcode=em20260620-1&t=1023&akid=7301%2E582294%2EWa3rBm ]Will you

Our next steps will decide whether we can keep up, respond to attacks, and
reach the voters we need to win. I’m counting on your grassroots support.

Thanks for being with me,

Chris

Mississippi has a new set of eyes on its roads -- and most residents have no idea they're coming.
The Mississippi Department of Information Technology Services Board quietly approved a contract last week with an Australian company called Acusensus to deploy AI-powered surveillance cameras on state roadways. The contract is worth $2,052,000 over three years, paid for entirely through federal grants. No legislative debate. No public vote. A board approval and a press release.
The Magnolia Tribune broke the story Thursday, and the details deserve a closer look.
**What These Cameras Actually Do**
Acusensus makes a product called Heads-Up. It is not a speed camera, and it is not a red light camera. It is something more sweeping than either.
The system works from mobile trailers that can be parked anywhere on the road network -- left unattended for days or weeks at a time -- and photographs every single vehicle that passes. Not vehicles it suspects. Not vehicles flagged by an officer. Every vehicle. The company's own materials describe it as capturing "all traffic flow in the enforced lanes." The AI then analyzes each image, looking simultaneously for a phone in a driver's hand, an unbuckled seatbelt, a speeding vehicle, or an out-of-service registration.
When the AI flags a potential violation, it sends a real-time alert to a law enforcement officer waiting downstream. That officer then pulls your car over and issues a citation -- for something he never personally witnessed.
The Mississippi Department of Public Safety's own representative explained the process to the ITS Board: "The AI will actually capture it and send it downstream to an officer sitting downstream. The officer will determine if it is a valid violation for a stop and at that point the officer will actually stop the car and issue a citation in real-time."
State Rep. Dan Eubanks (R) identified the constitutional problem immediately. "Every American citizen has a Constitutional right to face his or her accuser," he said. "This begs the question, is that accuser some ambiguous AI positioned and aimed to stare into your vehicle... or the officer who didn't physically witness the offense but is now writing you the ticket or making the arrest at the behest of that Artificial Intelligence?"
**What Mississippi Law Currently Says**
Before you accept the premise that these cameras are simply enforcing the law, it helps to understand what Mississippi law actually requires of drivers.
Mississippi banned texting while driving in **2015** -- one of the last states in the country to do so. House Bill 389, signed by Governor Phil Bryant, prohibits writing, sending, or reading a text, email, or social media post on a handheld device while driving. The fine is $100. As of July 1, 2026, it counts as a traffic violation on your record rather than a civil penalty.
But here is the critical detail: **Mississippi has no law against holding a phone.** Talking on a phone while driving -- phone held to your ear -- is completely legal in Mississippi. The Legislature drew a deliberate line: texting is prohibited, holding the phone is not.
An AI camera cannot see that line. It sees a hand near a phone and flags it as a potential violation. It cannot distinguish between a driver who is texting -- which is illegal -- and a driver who is making a hands-free call with the phone resting in their hand -- which is legal. The officer downstream receives an AI flag for behavior the camera cannot legally classify.
**Mississippi Already Banned These Kinds of Cameras Once**
This is not Mississippi's first encounter with automated traffic enforcement. In 2009, the Legislature passed House Bill 1568 by a near-unanimous vote -- 111-9 in the House, 42-9 in the Senate -- banning counties and municipalities from using automated cameras to detect traffic violations. Governor Haley Barbour signed it into law. Jackson and Columbus, the two cities that already had red light cameras at the time, were required to remove them by October 1 of that year.
The 2009 law was a direct response to the same concerns now being raised about Acusensus: cameras issuing citations without an officer present, government revenue dressed up as public safety, and the fundamental question of whether automated enforcement belongs on public roads.
The Acusensus contract appears to sidestep that law on a technicality. The 2009 ban covers county and municipal governments -- not state agencies. The Mississippi Department of Public Safety is a state agency. The trailer-based cameras also move constantly, arguably avoiding the "installed" standard in the law's definition.
The letter of the 2009 law may not reach this contract. But its spirit could not be clearer.
**The Question Mississippians Should Be Asking**
Mississippi's Legislature told cities they could not use cameras to enforce traffic laws. Seventeen years later, the state's own agency has contracted to do exactly that -- scanning every driver on targeted corridors, flagging potential violations by algorithm, and directing officers to make stops the officers never independently initiated.
House Ways and Means Chairman Trey Lamar said after learning of the contract that he expects the Legislature to investigate. That investigation is overdue and should happen before a single camera goes up.

subject: Peter, I’m the Democrat running against Virginia Foxx

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ch.email?refcode=onboarding [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ch.email?refcode=onboarding]
Peter,
If we haven’t met before, I’m Chuck Hubbard. I’m a native of northwestern North Carolina who's spent forty years of my career working in local journalism, and I'm also the Democrat running for Congress to unseat Virginia Foxx.
(You may remember her from when she screamed at a reporter to shut up earlier this year [https://thehill.com/homenews/house/4274345-republican-tells-reporter-to-shut-up-johnson-2020-election/] . As a former journalist myself, I took that one personally.)
Chuck Hubbard headshot [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/107748/images/ChuckHeadshot2.jpg]
These mountains have been my home all my life. I've spent most of my adult life working at the local paper my granddaddy built, and I always put my community first—and that's exactly why I made the decision to take a leap and run for this seat. I’m proud to say that I never once let my political beliefs influence my reporting, and in Congress, I’ll take that same mindset, rejecting political theater and focusing on what’s important—improving the lives of the folks back home.
But I’m also running because my opponent, Virginia Foxx, is one of the most dangerous Republicans you may have never heard of.
She’s an ultra-conservative Trump loyalist whose MAGA agenda is too extreme for North Carolina. As Chairwoman of the Committee on Education and the Workforce, she's been the Republican Party's main architect for dismantling public education and workers’ protections as we know it. I've watched her rise to power with a journalists' eye, and I've never once seen her put people before politics, or even before her own ambition.
Peter, I refuse to sit back and watch any longer as Virginia Foxx and Republicans in Congress ignore the needs of our neighbors, only focusing on their extremist social legislation and anti-worker policies. That’s not the North Carolina way, and we have a duty to stand up and fight it—and to stand up and fight for rural voters.
My campaign is going to get out into every single county, and we’re going to do whatever we can to reach every single voter and make sure they know we care, we’re fighting for them, and we value their votes.
But I'll be honest: this isn't going to be easy. If we're going to stand a chance of winning, then I really need your support, Peter. If you’re able to, please consider making a contribution of $25, $50 or anything you can, in support of our campaign's effort to beat Virginia Foxx and flip this district blue. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ch.email?refcode=onboarding]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ch.email?refcode=onboarding]
If we stand together, we’ll have the resources to spread the Democratic message to every corner of my district—we’ll be able to fund a real campaign operation so that I can spend my time knocking doors, turning out and talking with every Democrat and Unaffiliated voter I possibly can! I know it’s an uphill fight, Peter, but I never met anybody who climbed a mountain by not trying.
Chuck Hubbard headshot [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/107748/images/IMG_0462.png] Thanks for standing with me,
Chuck Hubbard
Democrat for Congress

Peter, I refuse to sit back and watch any longer as Virginia Foxx and Republicans in Congress ignore the needs of our neighbors, only focusing on their extremist social legislation and anti-worker policies. That’s not the North Carolina way, and we have a duty to stand up and fight it—and to stand up and fight for rural voters. My campaign is going to get out into every single county, and we’re going to do whatever we can to reach every single voter and make sure they know we care, we’re fighting for them, and we value their votes. But I'll be honest: this isn't going to be easy. If we're going to stand a chance of winning, then I really need your support, Peter. If you’re able to, please consider making a contribution of $25, $50 or anything you can, in support of our campaign's effort to beat Virginia Foxx and flip this district blue. [] DONATE NOW [] If we stand together, we’ll have the resources to spread the Democratic message to every corner of my district—we’ll be able to fund a real campaign operation so that I can spend my time knocking doors, turning out and talking with every Democrat and Unaffiliated voter I possibly can! I know it’s an uphill fight, Peter, but I never met anybody who climbed a mountain by not trying. body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| Letter from the Chair
---
Momentum Building: Together, We Win!
As many of you know, Nebraska Republicans gathered in La Vista for our State Convention and left standing behind a full slate of nominees and one clear mission: Get Out the Vote. That energy hasn't faded. If anything, it's sharpened.
Much of that momentum traces back to a single moment at convention: when our federal and statewide candidates took the stage together, side by side, making clear this is one team running on one mission. That kind of visible togetherness doesn't happen by accident, and delegates noticed. It set the tone for everything since. Since convention, our Republican candidates have been on the move, talking to voters, building coalitions, and making the case for Nebraska values in every corner of the state. The theme that rang through the convention hall, "Together, We Win!", isn't a slogan we packed up and put away. It's the operating plan for the summer ahead.
This is the part of the cycle where the real work happens. Conventions generate energy. Summer is where that energy turns into doors knocked, calls made, and voters reached. Every county party, every precinct captain, every volunteer matters more right now than at almost any other point in the calendar.
Our nominees are ready to fight for Nebraska. Now it's on all of us to make sure every voter knows it.
Nebraska Republicans Won't Be Fooled
As the general election field comes into focus, one thing remains certain: Nebraska Republicans will continue to reject so-called "pseudo-Independents" and "Nonpartisans" who try to bypass our party's nomination process to sneak onto the general election ballot.
If a candidate cannot face Republican voters in a Primary, they are unlikely to earn their support in November. Why hide behind petition signatures instead of standing before county party members, defending your positions, and earning the trust of those who do the real work?
The easiest thing in politics is getting your name on a ballot. File some paperwork. Gather a handful of signatures. The hard part, the honorable part, is earning the respect of grassroots Republicans by showing up at county meetings, working the precincts, and proving yourself in the trenches long before your name ever appears anywhere.
We've seen this play before. A candidate skips the Primary, skips the scrutiny, skips the accountability, and then asks for votes in November as if none of that matters. It does matter. The process exists for a reason: it tests candidates, it earns trust, and it builds the kind of grassroots support that actually wins elections. Bypassing it isn't a shortcut to legitimacy. It's an admission that a candidate couldn't survive the real test.
True conservatives don't run from scrutiny. They embrace it.
Nebraska Republicans see through these tactics every time. We stand firmly behind our duly nominated candidates, in word and in deed. Real change comes through the Republican Party, not around it. And as petition deadlines and ballot announcements roll in over the coming weeks, we'll be watching closely and calling it out every time we see it.
Let's keep carrying the momentum from our State Convention through a strong summer of voter outreach. Together, we will win in 2026 and keep delivering results for Nebraska families. Forward together!

In Liberty and in Truth, Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

| State Senator Spotlight, Senator Rick Holdcroft - LD 36
Parents know what is best for their children - not the government. As a father and grandpa, I understand the importance of keeping parents involved in their children's lives. But out-of-touch politicians and government bureaucrats have attempted to put government at the center of children's lives.
When I was elected, I promised I would stand for faith, family, and freedom. That's why I'm fighting every day to protect common sense and keep parents in charge of raising their children. In the Legislature, I worked hand in hand with fellow Republican Senators to keep big tech companies from influencing and guiding children's lives without parental involvement.
Parents deserve transparency and accountability from schools, government agencies, and big tech companies. Moms and dads deserve to know what their children are being taught, what content they are being exposed to online, and who is influencing them. The government should support parents - not replace them.

As many of you know, Nebraska Republicans gathered in La Vista for our State Convention and left standing behind a full slate of nominees and one clear mission: Get Out the Vote. body:

# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
The “Summer Slump” is something political campaigns face every single year.
School is officially out for the summer, the sun is shining, families are heading out on well-deserved vacations, and fundraising numbers across the board always take a sudden dip.
It’s a phenomenon we’ve come to expect. But we do need to explain why a "Summer Slump" is such a massive risk for us right now, especially with Election Day just 5 months away.
**[Before we dive into the explanation, will you pitch in $5 to Gina’s campaign today to keep our momentum steady?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260620_1_summer.3j2U5a&refcode=em20260620-1382&amount=5&t=1&akid=1382%2E299639%2EIDecVe)**
Falling short during the summer months is dangerous because it directly threatens our ability to do three important things:
* **Meet voters where they are:** We need the resources to stay out on the trail, travel the state, and share Gina’s vision.
* **Hit our fundraising goals:** Missing our summer goals means we fall further behind Greg Abbott’s multi-million-dollar war chest.
* **Secure our airtime early:** We have to invest in digital ads right now before the fall rush, when ad space becomes incredibly scarce and expensive.

Summer is easily the most challenging stretch of this campaign — but it is also the most critical window to build a winning campaign.
**[Peter, will you make a $5 donation or any amount you can to help us beat this summer slump?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260620_1_summer.3j2U5a&refcode=em20260620-1382&amount=5&t=2&akid=1382%2E299639%2EIDecVe)**

Team Gina

Peter — There is nothing the powerful special interests in Florida want more than to watch our campaign fail and keep the status quo exactly as it is. **How do I know? Because I’ve been their target before.** As a state senator, I was one of the few people in Tallahassee consistently standing up to Florida Power & Light on behalf of its customers. I filed legislation to break their grip and give families more control over their own power. FPL's CEO was so furious that he told his own executives to make my life _"a living hell."_ They didn't stop at threats. **When I ran for re-election in 2020, Republican operatives bribed a ghost candidate — _someone with my exact same last name_ — **to run against me and pull votes away. It worked. The voters were the real victims of that scheme, but I was the target. What they did wasn't just corrupt — it was criminal, and the man behind the scheme was convicted. But Peter, I'm not telling you this for sympathy. I'm telling you because it's the clearest proof of what we're up against, and why I'm running for Attorney General. These same powerful special interests are still winning. **FPL just secured the largest rate hike in its history from state regulators, and Uthmeier didn't lift a finger to stop it.** In other states, attorneys general fight these increases, sue the utilities, and recover money for families. Florida hasn’t had an Attorney General willing to stand up to powerful special interests in decades. **[I will. clean_body: And they'll do anything to keep the status quo. | Peter — There is nothing the powerful special interests in Florida want more than to watch our campaign fail and keep the status quo exactly as it is. How do I know? Because I’ve been their target before. As a state senator, I was one of the few people in Tallahassee consistently standing up to Florida Power & Light on behalf of its customers. I filed legislation to break their grip and give families more control over their own power. FPL's CEO was so furious that he told his own executives to make my life "a living hell." They didn't stop at threats. When I ran for re-election in 2020, Republican operatives bribed a ghost candidate — someone with my exact same last name — to run against me and pull votes away. It worked. The voters were the real victims of that scheme, but I was the target. What they did wasn't just corrupt — it was criminal, and the man behind the scheme was convicted. But Peter, I'm not telling you this for sympathy. I'm telling you because it's the clearest proof of what we're up against, and why I'm running for Attorney General. These same powerful special interests are still winning. FPL just secured the largest rate hike in its history from state regulators, and Uthmeier didn't lift a finger to stop it. In other states, attorneys general fight these increases, sue the utilities, and recover money for families. Republicans have made it clear: fighting for you is not on their agenda.
They aren’t trying to pass legislation to make groceries or housing or gas more affordable. They aren’t concerned with holding Donald Trump (the self-proclaimed “Peace President”) accountable for his illegal and unnecessary wars. They aren’t interested in reining in Trump’s sweeping tariffs that have made life way too expensive.
Instead, this Congress has become another arm of the Oval Office. We only pass the bills that Trump supports — and when the GOP doesn’t have the votes to get it done, they call a recess until enough members are harassed and bullied into submission.
This is not how government is supposed to work.
When Democrats flip the House in the fall, we set the agenda. Our majority will get us back to the business of making sure that we are putting the people first. Not the President. Not corporations. Not billionaire CEOs. Not tech oligarchs. You.
But we can’t win back the House without putting in the work. If you can, will you contribute $25 to help me get re-elected and get us closer to a Democratic majority? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/suhas-em=true&amount=25]
