As an instructor in Georgia State’s nursing school, I’ve spent years teaching and supporting the students who keep our healthcare system alive. I know how hard they work, how much they sacrifice, and how urgently our state needs more advanced practice nurses — not fewer.
So when I saw this headline...
https://secure.ngpvan.com/4OI02pK92kOTd_uWTjBgFg2 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/4OI02pK92kOTd_uWTjBgFg2]
...I felt sick.
Under Donald Trump’s new proposal, advanced nursing degrees would no longer count as “professional,” meaning students would lose access to the federal loans they need to pursue graduate education. Loan limits would be slashed in half. Thousands of future nurse practitioners, nurse midwives, CRNAs, and clinical nurse specialists could be forced to take on massive private debt — or give up their dreams entirely.
This is not just bad policy.
It’s dangerous — for patients, for hospitals, and for the future of healthcare in this country.
Georgia already faces provider shortages. Rural communities already wait weeks for care. And now Trump wants to create even fewer advanced practice nurses?
We cannot allow this to go unanswered.
The American Nurses Association has already sounded the alarm, and more than 200,000 nurses and patients have raised their voices. Now I’m asking you to add yours:
Will you sign the petition demanding the Department of Education reverse this reckless decision and recognize advanced nursing degrees as the professional degrees they are? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/4OI02pK92kOTd_uWTjBgFg2]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://secure.ngpvan.com/4OI02pK92kOTd_uWTjBgFg2]
Our nurses deserve respect. Our students deserve opportunity. And our healthcare system deserves investment — not sabotage.
Thank you for standing up for science, for students, and for the people who keep us healthy.

body:
Chris Pappas is in a tied race — and Republicans are coming for this seat.

Hi, it’s Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear.
There’s a lot of noise in an election year — I know that better than most. But let me be very clear: **The Senate race in New Hampshire could decide the direction of this country.**
Chris Pappas is running in a tied race. It could be a toss-up. And with Donald Trump in the White House, the stakes couldn’t be higher.
**[That’s why I’m asking you to donate right now to help Chris Pappas win.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260620_2.QroaII&refcode=em20260620-2&t=2&akid=7303%2E582294%2EP9IJEq)**
The first year of this second Trump Administration has seen chaos, division, and dangerous rollbacks of basic freedoms. That’s why it’s so important that we elect leaders like Chris Pappas — leaders who know how to bring people together, deliver real results, and who will never forget who they’re fighting for.
Chris’s opponent is a former U.S. Senator with national name recognition and the backing of national Republicans and their deep-pocketed super PACs. Republicans believe they can flip this seat and block any chance that we have of checking Trump’s power in Washington.
But I believe in Chris — and I believe we can win.
Chris understands that leadership isn’t about grabbing headlines or scoring political points. It’s about showing up, listening, and doing the hard work to deliver for working families. He’s done that in Congress, and I know he’ll bring that same spirit of public service to the Senate.
Kentucky and New Hampshire may look different, but our people want the same things: good jobs, strong public schools, access to health care, and a better future we can build together. That’s what Chris Pappas is fighting for. **_But he can’t do it alone._**
**[If you’re with me — and ready to stop Trump and his allies from flipping this critical seat — contribute now to help Chris Pappas win.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260620_2.QroaII&refcode=em20260620-2&t=3&akid=7303%2E582294%2EP9IJEq)**

| A new FEC report has just been released, and we now have a clearer look at who is directly funding my opponent, Diana DeGette, in the final days of this campaign.
💰 Nearly $700,000 from PACs and political committees. Novartis. Amgen. AbbVie. Pfizer. UnitedHealth Group. Cigna. Blue Cross Blue Shield. DaVita. Labcorp. The list goes on and on.
💸 Almost $400,000 appears to come from healthcare, pharmaceutical, insurance, and medical industry PACs alone.
It's rich because just last night, at a forum in front of Denver voters, Diana claimed it doesn't matter that she takes corporate PAC money, since her votes cannot be bought, and that if voters send her back to Congress, this time, she will "pass" Medicare for All.
I'm sorry, but come on...
Why would Big Pharma and the health care industry pour hundreds of thousands of dollars into her campaign if they believed she was actually going to pass legislation that would threaten their profits?
Why would the same corporations making billions off our broken health care system spend so much money to keep her in Congress if they were afraid she would finally take them on? 🧐
The ONLY thing adding up here is the money she is accepting from corporate PACs.
This is exactly what is wrong with our politics. Politicians accept corporate PAC checks for decades, then stand before voters and promise that this time will be different. This time, they will fight the industries that fund them and finally deliver!
But working families in Denver are still getting buried by medical debt, and people are rationing care. Prescription drug companies have become increasingly obscene under her 30-year watch, and insurance companies are denying claims at climbing rates.
I am not taking corporate PAC money.
Not from Big Pharma, the health insurance industry, or the other corporate PACs Diana accepts checks from - like ICE contractors and weapons makers.
When I go to Congress, I want there to be no confusion about who I work for.

Hi Peter,
John Willoughby here – proud husband of Rep. Kelly Morrison. Last week, we celebrated our 29th wedding anniversary. Across nearly three decades of marriage, so much has happened – navigating career shifts, raising three wonderful children, and supporting Kelly as she stepped up to run for office!
During her first campaign in 2018, I tagged along to a campaign event with her. Kelly introduced herself and gave her stump speech, and when she wrapped up a man in the front row raised his and asked the following question:
“You seem like a nice lady. But will you be tough enough when the Republicans come after you?
Peter, we all know the answer to that — Kelly Morrison is pretty damn tough.
I was with her at the Whipple Federal Building this winter. And I have never been more proud than when she marched past the protestors, past the security guards, and right up to the armed ICE agents and demanded to be let in to conduct oversight.
I have watched Kelly, time and time again, call out this administration’s barrage of misinformation around healthcare. She uses her deep understanding of evidence-based policy to get her point across, and never misses the opportunity to ensure we know the truth.
Kelly will not let this Republican trifecta at the top stop her. She was the first freshman Democrat to pass a bill on the House floor, and has passed a number of bills since. It is not easy, but she knows how to get things done to improve people’s lives. No one cares more, and no one works harder.
Kelly demonstrates real, effective leadership. She is exactly who we need in Congress. And she needs our help.
In just a few weeks, we are approaching our second end of quarter fundraising deadline of this election year. We need to raise just about $22,000 to meet our goal and close our budget gap.
Peter, can you chip in any amount TODAY to help us get there?

subject: Fighting to protect public education
body:
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
**Gina recently launched Team Texas Public Schools** , new bipartisan organizing program designed to engage parents, teachers, and administrators — regardless of party — to fight school closures across the state.
**[Peter, if you support public education and want to help fuel our fight to protect education for all Texas kids, will you rush a donation of $5 today?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260620_2_ttps.yqdNbF&refcode=em20260620-1384&amount=5&t=1&akid=1384%2E299639%2ErUmp00)**
Gina has seen what our public schools can do when they’re properly supported, and she has seen exactly what happens when politicians rig the system against them.
The truth is, Gina first ran for office as a mom because politicians were threatening to shut down her son’s neighborhood school. She locked arms with neighbors, built a community coalition, and **they won that fight.**
In Texas, Greg Abbott has been threatening Texas public education at every single turn. For the last decade we’ve seen him:
* Over-test our kids
* Undermine our teachers and drive people away from the profession
* Defund our neighborhood schools, forcing campuses to consider closures and pushing rural districts onto four-day weeks
* Hand public dollars to private interests through a voucher scheme with absolutely no real accountability

**Texas kids deserve so much better, Peter. Plain and simple.**
Gina is running for governor because she knows we can deliver on the true promise of public education. When she is elected, we are going to end the era of the high-stakes STAAR test. We are going to roll back Abbott’s voucher scheme that funnels your hard-earned taxpayer dollars into private academies, and we’re going to ensure Texas educators are properly paid.
Our neighborhood schools are essential to the American Dream, but they cannot survive another four years of being starved of resources by Greg Abbott.
If you believe that every single student in Texas deserves a well-funded public education system, Gina is standing right there with you. That’s the future she will fight for every single day as our next governor.
**[Will you pitch in $5 or anything you can afford today to support Team Texas Public Schools, defeat Greg Abbott this November, and protect public education?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260620_2_ttps.yqdNbF&refcode=em20260620-1384&amount=5&t=2&akid=1384%2E299639%2ErUmp00)**

Thank you,
Team Gina

They say this district is too red. Too independent. Too easy for national extremists to take over if they just spend enough money and say the same scary things loudly enough.
Well, they said that before 2022, too. We won anyway.

Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

A message that reminds the world that every child has God-given dignity. And importantly, a message that sparks conversations and helps raise awareness about a crisis many people still do not see. A story of faith lost, tested, and found again | | | |
---
| | | Fellow Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

clean_body: A story of faith lost, tested, and found again | | | | | | | Fellow Patriot, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Fellow Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith. Your support does far more than just send you a book... It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack. Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God. For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed. And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change -- and so do their lives. Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for. He believed young people were not beyond reach -- they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly. That's why your support matters. It helps Turning Point USA keep showing up. And it helps carry forward the mission Charlie gave his life to build. | | | Now's the time to act. Now's the time to restore faith in God and faith in America before another generation drifts even farther from both. And with you, Charlie's mission will reach further -- and touch more young lives -- than ever before. For Charlie, The Turning Point USA Team P.S. Fellow Patriot, many young people leave home with a foundation of faith, only to have the culture chip away at it, piece by piece. JD Vance knows what that struggle looks like. So do countless young Americans who Turning Point USA is reaching right now. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...

**We 're in 3,300 schools. **

**Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. **

**Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. **

_That shouldn 't be possible. _

Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day.

And yet... it's still happening.

_But Peter, here 's the part you need to understand: _

This is not a victory. It's a foothold.

_Because in the other 87% of schools? _

There is no resistance. None.

Just one-sided propaganda from the Left.

One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them.

That's the reality.

The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are.

The question is whether it's enough.

Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America...

They're not the majority. _They 're the exception. _

They're the ones willing to take the heat.

The ones willing to stand alone.

The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: _" I love this country." _

Everything they need to actually stand their ground.

Not symbolically. For real.

They've already made the decision to lead.

All they're waiting on... is you and me.

**Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. **

Not "if things keep going this way." Right now. And the scariest part? It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms. High schools. Colleges. Election analysts at The New York Times recently reported that North Carolina is the best chance in the country for Democrats to flip a Republican-held seat. 2\. That’s why GOP dark-money super PACs are so far investing nearly $100 million to spread lies about me in baseless attack ads and crush our grassroots momentum. 3\. This race is a toss-up. My job is to lead the staff of this organization and make sure we have the budget, resources, and strategy we need to elect Democratic pro-choice women at every level of government. I want to be very direct about why that matters. EMILYs List was founded because women candidates were not getting the early support they needed to run credible, competitive campaigns. Ellen Malcolm and a group of groundbreaking women knew that if women were going to win elections, they needed early money, real fundraising power, and a donor network that believed in them before the political establishment caught up. That is why EMILYs List exists. And from the very beginning, this work was about people willing to invest early — people who understood that money is not just money in a campaign. It is credibility. It is staff. It is voter contact. It is the difference between being written off and being taken seriously — between winning and losing. = | = The history of EMILYs List matters, but I am writing today because our work and mission cannot just exist in the past. The work we do matters more than ever right now. Every day, our staff is working to recruit, train, support, and elect Democratic pro-choice women who can change the direction of this country. Our team is helping candidates build stronger campaigns. We are raising the money they need to compete. We are studying races, voters, issues, and opposition. We are communicating with millions of supporters about what is at stake. We are running paid programs to help our candidates win in some of the most competitive races in the country. And behind every email, every endorsement, and every strategic decision is a team of people who are very, very good at what they do. I will say this plainly: This is the best team in politics. Where we’re combating the national redistricting crisis on the ballot this fall.
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133703643/628782536/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjhjNzBmYzE5LWU0NmMtZjExMS04ZmNiLTAwMGQzYTE0YjZkNiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ENxTtjrY16HxPY_m5ewlr20XMCyksr4mss2ThLiQPMk=&emci=84db6d63-3f6b-f111-8fcb-000d3a18905c&emdi=8c70fc19-e46c-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b6d6&ceid=8431045)
---

Peter, you probably don’t need me to tell you this, but a lot is riding on this year’s elections. **That’s why the NDRC is rolling out an aggressive campaign plan — focused on 14 priority states** whose elections are key to stopping Republican gerrymanders and putting more states in a position to pass countermeasures or block future map manipulation. The entire country just got an up-close look at how impactful these state-level elections can be. We’ve seen how just a few more pro-democracy voices in a legislative body can stop a mid-decade redraw. We’ve seen how partisan courts can put their thumbs on the scale. And we’ve seen how Republicans have abused their power in states where they hold a trifecta: control of the governor’s office as well as both chambers of the state legislature. **The other side knows how critical these elections are, too — the GOP’s 2026 targets are centered on getting an upper hand in the redistricting crisis.** They have a wish list of legislatures and governorships they want to take over, all so they can keep rigging district lines to stockpile power for 2028 and beyond. | We’re building on a track record of success — from supreme court races in Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, and North Carolina to critical Virginia elections last fall. Our investments will aim to support three goals:
1. Electing Democrats for governor, state legislature, and other key state-level offices that play a major role in the redistricting process.
2. Combating partisan efforts to reduce the independence of the state supreme courts by supporting fair-minded judges.
3. Enacting ballot initiatives to counter Republican gerrymandering or overturn GOP redraws.

---

clean_body: Where we’re combating the national redistricting crisis on the ballot this fall. | Peter, you probably don’t need me to tell you this, but a lot is riding on this year’s elections. That’s why the NDRC is rolling out an aggressive campaign plan — focused on 14 priority states whose elections are key to stopping Republican gerrymanders and putting more states in a position to pass countermeasures or block future map manipulation. The entire country just got an up-close look at how impactful these state-level elections can be. We’ve seen how just a few more pro-democracy voices in a legislative body can stop a mid-decade redraw. We’ve seen how partisan courts can put their thumbs on the scale. And we’ve seen how Republicans have abused their power in states where they hold a trifecta: control of the governor’s office as well as both chambers of the state legislature. The other side knows how critical these elections are, too — the GOP’s 2026 targets are centered on getting an upper hand in the redistricting crisis. They have a wish list of legislatures and governorships they want to take over, all so they can keep rigging district lines to stockpile power for 2028 and beyond. | We’re building on a track record of success — from supreme court races in Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, and North Carolina to critical Virginia elections last fall. Our investments will aim to support three goals: 1. Electing Democrats for governor, state legislature, and other key state-level offices that play a major role in the redistricting process. 2. Combating partisan efforts to reduce the independence of the state supreme courts by supporting fair-minded judges. 3. Enacting ballot initiatives to counter Republican gerrymandering or overturn GOP redraws. It’s one thing to talk about fighting back. Friend: In a moment, I'm going to share with you my vision for New Mexico — **_[but first, can I ask you to take 30 seconds to personally endorse my campaign for Governor?](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202606_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk915-su-nd&refcode=jtk915-su-nd&t=2&akid=10391%2E400544%2E_UxT9n)_**

---
This message is a bit on the longer side, but because you're invested in the future of New Mexico, I hope you'll take the time to read my plan. **As New Mexico’s next Governor, I will:**
**Build Education That Works for New Mexico by:**
* Ensuring students can read before third grade by identifying literacy challenges early and providing targeted support when children fall behind

* Strengthening early literacy screening, expanding bilingual and reading instruction, and investing in summer reading and after-school programs that reinforce learning beyond the school day

* Bolstering access to universal childcare, because learning begins long before a child enters a classroom

* Directing unspent dollars from the Public School Capital Outlay Fund to modernize and improve school facilities so kids can focus on learning

* Expanding outdoor and place-based learning through my Every Child Outdoor Initiative, giving schools the tools and resources to connect classroom instruction to real-world learning that improves engagement and outcomes

**Support New Mexico Families by:**
* Raising the minimum wage and eliminating predatory junk fees

* Passing Paid Family and Medical Leave so people don’t have to choose between caring for their family and making ends meet

* Increasing the child tax credit to put money back into your pockets

* Creating a statewide tenant bill of rights to make renting more affordable and more transparent

* Creating a Critical Sector Housing Fund for workers in critical sectors — like healthcare, behavioral health, social work, education, and more — to recruit more professionals to New Mexico to address endemic shortages that hold our people back

* Aggressively building more housing, eliminating unnecessary red tape, driving state investment into housing, and shortening the time it takes to build a home — and ensuring those homes are built with New Mexican labor

**Back Small Businesses by:**
* Establishing a permanent Office of Small Business to coordinate development programs, fill gaps left by federal cuts, and provide clear access to grants, capital, and state resources

* Cracking down on predatory lending by requiring full transparency in small-business loan disclosures

* Establishing a New Mexico Economic Growth Trust Fund to stabilize our economy in the face of federal uncertainty

**Fix Our Broken Healthcare System by:**
* Protecting and expanding access to healthcare in every part of New Mexico

* Banning medical debt from being included on credit reports

* Expanding New Mexico’s Health Care Affordability Fund to protect access for those who rely on the state marketplace

* Using budget surpluses to fill Medicaid gaps and hire more guides to help people enroll in and keep their benefits

* Ensuring sustainable funding for rural hospitals and clinics, expanding mobile health clinics, and significantly increasing access to outpatient behavioral and mental health care, including a full-scale effort to deliver mental health and homelessness assistance statewide

**Strengthen Public Safety by:**
* Ensuring that law enforcement has the tools, staffing, and technology they need to do their jobs effectively

* Investing in mental and behavioral healthcare and housing stability

* Expanding violence intervention and prevention programs in schools and communities, building accountability systems that emphasize fairness and trust, and investing in community policing models that supplement traditional police work

* Creating a statewide Department of Community Safety staffed with social workers and counselors so law enforcement can focus on violent crime while people get the help they need

* Requiring ICE agents to clearly identify themselves and prohibiting masks that shield misconduct from accountability

New Mexico deserves steady leadership that’s ready on day one, leadership rooted in firsthand knowledge and experience. But the only way we'll be able to make this vision a reality is with strong grassroots support from people like you.
**I'm aiming to get 10,000 endorsements for my campaign before my midnight deadline to show the grassroots strength behind my vision for New Mexico, and I want you to be one of them._[Will you please take a quick moment to sign on now?](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202606_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk915-su-nd&refcode=jtk915-su-nd&t=4&akid=10391%2E400544%2E_UxT9n)_**

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
# To My Dad on Father’s Day
---
| |
Dear Dad,
Thank you!

Your sacrifices deserve more than praise and appreciation. Your commitment to God, your family, and this country has earned you a chance to rest. However, your investment in the Social Security trust fund has been stolen. The money they took out of every one of your paychecks has been spent.
I love you too much to not go fight for what you paid for.
Sadly, the men and women you voted to lead and protect you don't follow the same moral compass. Even before you became a father and a husband, the country you love took a part of your income and issued a receipt with a promise. A promise they've broken. Not just once - 2.5 trillion times and counting.
The Social Security trust fund you've paid into your entire life will be insolvent in 72 months. They've taken your money and given it to other people and government programs. Additionally, the Congresspersons who've promised to save Social Security in every election since before you were born have taken 2.5 trillion dollars out of the "TRUST" fund they swore to not only improve but protect. They've politically manipulated your investment by calling it an entitlement. This isn't a government issued right.
It's simply getting what you paid for.

There is no business in the entire world that stays in business very long that takes our money and, in return, DOESN'T give us the product or a service we paid for. Yet, our Congress says “Sorry and don't forget to vote for me again”. Service is not based on who you are but who you are for.

I'm a dad who strives to be the example you taught me to be for my children, your grandchildren. But we can't ensure their future if we don't protect our past. I'm sorry, Dad, your job is not done yet. I need you, and a lot of other dads, to tell the liars and thieves “your reign is over” and help me get elected to office.
Exodus 20:12 says: "Honor your father and mother, so that you may live long in the land the Lord is giving you."
Dad, help me go honor you and all the other fathers and mothers in this land God has given us. The clock is ticking. We need you, Dad, and all dads to **VOTE FOR ME ON AUGUST 11TH.**
Can we afford to continue to trust the same broken promise-keepers?

Your son,
Austin Sidwell
A father willing to fight for the country you taught me to love.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
## **This Campaign Runs on Grit, Faith, and Folks Like You.**

Career politicians have million-dollar machines behind them.
I don’t.
This campaign is powered by hardworking Alabamians who believe faith, family, and freedom are worth fighting for.
Every donation helps us reach more voters, challenge the establishment, and take our message across South Alabama.
Please chip in today and help prove that the people—not the political elites—still decide our elections.

| **GOVERNMENT CLOSER TO THE PEOPLE**
---
|
---
| Hi friends,Recently, Kelly and I spent time in Carbon, Laramie, Albany, Campbell, and Fremont Counties.In Carbon, Laramie, and Albany Counties, we spent time with community members from Elk Mountain, Rawlins, Saratoga, Savery, Baggs, Dixon, Encampment, Riverside, Cheyenne, Albin, Pine Bluffs, and Laramie talking about reclamiation, water rights and the Colorado River Compact, local development, the University of Wyoming including CTE and the WWAMI programs, the Wyoming Business Council, property taxes and thier importance to many of our essential services, senior and rural healthcare, and the need to bring more civility back into politics. In Cheyenne, I met with the Wyoming Coroner's Association. I am still not sure why this is a partisan elected office.Everywhere we go, I am reminded that Wyoming works because people care enough to show up. They serve meals. They teach kids. They take care of seniors. They build businesses, work the land, produce energy, protect our communities, and help their neighbors without making a fuss about it.That is also why state government has to do a better job staying connected to the people it serves. I recently announced a plan to establish regional organize the Governor’s Office with regional representatives across Wyoming. This will give communities have a more direct line to the Governor’s Office and so the state can hear about problems earlier, respond more quickly, and better understand what is happening on the ground.For a lot of folks, Cheyenne can feel a long way off. I believe government works best when it is close enough to listen and humble enough to learn from the people doing the work every day.I spent Friday and Saturday in Campbell County. It was Wright Days, where small-town Wyoming was on full display with good food, good company, and neighbors gathering together. That is the Wyoming Kelly and I know and love.Kelly spent the end of the week at the State Convention for P.E.O. in Lander. Kelly believes deeply in service in her everyday. P.E.O. is one of her philanthropic organizations and is women who motivate, educate and celebrate women. During the state convention, my mom, Bernie, was recognized for being in P.E.O. for 50 years and Kelly assumed the role as Vice President for the Wyoming State Chapter. I am so proud of both of them and glad I was able to join for the family dinner Saturday evening.Forums, parades, fairs, and summer community celebrations are just getting started. I participated in a few this past week and when I was unable to go, campaign volunteers and staff showed up to help do the work and be a party of these important community events. Be sure to say hi if you see us in your town. Thank you for being part of this campaign.-EricRiding for Wyoming,

| **IN CASE YOU MISSED IT** **Eric Barlow Calls for More Responsive, Accessible State Government** LARAMIE, Wyo. — After months of traveling across Wyoming, Eric Barlow has heard the same message everywhere: people want a state government that is connected locally, listens and solves problems.Today at the Wyoming of Municipalities Gubernatorial Forum, Barlow announced a plan to establish five regional offices for the Governor across the state, bringing government closer to the people who need it.“Cheyenne can feel just as far away as Washington, D.C. for a lot of people in this state,” Barlow said. “Our Wyoming citizens are raising families, running businesses, working long hours, and living their lives. Government needs to do a better job getting out of the Capitol and into the communities it serves.”Barlow said that while Wyoming is proud of its citizen-led government, the distance can make it feel far away.Barlow’s proposal would create a more consistent regional presence for the Governor’s Office which should improve coordination on issues including economic development, infrastructure, local government concerns, agriculture, energy, health care access, emergency services, permitting, and workforce needs.Under Barlow’s plan, staff that would normally be located in Cheyenne, would instead be hired from the regional communities around the state, with the goal of making government work better by improving communication and identifying problems earlier, supported by staff that’s embedded and knows the area.“Government works best when it is closest to the people,” Barlow said. “The best solutions don’t come from the Capitol, but by the people doing the work every day in our communities.”Barlow said the proposal reflects the kind of leadership he believes Wyoming needs: practical, accessible, and rooted in service.Eric Barlow is a Campbell County rancher, large-animal veterinarian, Marine Corps veteran, and an effective and respectful Wyoming legislator running for Governor.

| **On The Trail**
---
| Before we share more from the road, Kelly and I want to offer our prayers and deep appreciation for Sgt. Burns, his family, the Carbon County Sheriff’s Office, and all of Wyoming’s first responders.Just the day before the tragic shooting in Baggs, we were in Savery visiting with first responders. The conversation was honest and wide-ranging, from property taxes and the pressure they place on local services, to what it means when rural communities have to look out for one another, including the men and women who answer the call when help is needed.Those conversations stay with you. In Wyoming, first responders are not strangers in uniform. They are our neighbors, parents, volunteers, coworkers, and friends. They serve in wide-open country, often with long distances, limited backup, and a deep commitment to the communities they call home.As we continue traveling the state, we are reminded again and again that Wyoming works best when we show up for one another. That was clear in Carbon County, and it has been clear in every community we have visited.
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **LANDER** Kelly was away from the campaign trail for a few days, spending time with what she calls “270ish of my favorite sisters” at the state PEO convention in Lander.It was extra special to see Eric’s mom Bernie receive recognition as a 50-year PEO member with her family by her side!
---
|
---
| | | **WRIGHT** Great time at Taste of Wright and the Wright Days Parade this weekend. Good food, and great company. Events like this are what small town Wyoming is all about. Thank you to everyone in Wright for the warm welcome.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **CHEYENNE** We had great visits last week at Life Care Center of Cheyenne and Pointe Frontier, two retirement communities here in Cheyenne. Always good to sit down with our seniors and hear their stories. So many discussions about how to keep Wyoming a place where we care about our neighbors and make sure their kids and grandkids can live in or come back to.
---
|
---
| | | **CHEYENNE** We had a great meet and greet at Uncle Charlie’s in Cheyenne. There was a great turnout with some new faces in the crowd. Good discussion on the balance of managing property taxes while still taking care of our communities. It is a real challenge and one Wyoming families think about every day. Thank you to everyone who came out
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **LARAMIE** It was a great morning with WWAMII young professionals, followed by a student luncheon in the afternoon. Wyoming’s future showed up in full from young professionals building careers here and students being recognized for their hard work and achievements
---
|
---
| | | **LARAMIE** We sat down with the Wyoming Association for Career and Technical Education summer conference, the annual ASRS (American Society of Reclamation Sciences) meeting, which just happened to be in Wyoming this year. The ASRS meeting included Jasmine Allison with PureWest Energy as the Reclamationist of the Year awardee and both the Pioneer of Reclamation awardees, who were Ron Schreibeis, retired from Rocky Mountain Reclamation LLC, and Kyle Wendtland with the Wyoming Energy Authority. Congratulations to all! And it just so happened that a few weeks ago, we met with Jasmine in the field, where she showed off her reclamation work. This is only the second time an oil and gas producer has been recognized with this award, and both were right here in Wyoming
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **ALBIN** We had a great event in Albin for a coffee meet and greet, and then we headed to Pine Bluffs to meet with town officials and tour a local development. Every community in Wyoming has its own story and its own set of opportunities. We are glad to be out listening and learning from the people closest to the work. Thank you to everyone who took time to visit with us
---
|
---
| | | **CHEYENNE** We started with a breakfast meet and greet at the R&B Breakfast Club, then visited Meals on Wheels, the Boys and Girls Club, and Girls State. Every stop a reminder of what makes Wyoming communities strong. The people showing up every day to take care of their neighbors and invest in the next generation. Grateful for the chance to see it firsthand
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **CHEYENNE** Kelly and I want to thank you, General Toby Alkire, and the Wyoming National Guard for the recognition you gave us while we were in Cheyenne. Back in July 2024, when the 2-300 Field Artillery Battalion was deploying from Gillette, we helped coordinate and sponsor a meal for the soldiers and their families at their farewell send-off. It was the least we could do for the men and women preparing to leave home and serve our country. Thank you to every soldier and family who was there that day.
---
|
---
| | | **RIVERSIDE & ENCAMPMENT**Kelly and I had a beautiful evening in Riverside, meeting with members of both the Riverside and Encampment communities, then made our way to Savery for a meet and greet at the Little Snake River Museum. Good conversation with community members from Savery, Baggs, and Dixon, including Eamon O’Toole, who is running for House District 47, and current Representative Bob Davis, who is running for Senate District 11.
The Little Snake River Museum is something special, a collection of buildings and exhibits that tell the story of this valley and the people who built it. The folks in Savery have a wealth of knowledge on the Colorado River Compact and sub-basin water law, and that kind of local expertise matters when decisions about Wyoming’s water future are being made.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **SARATOGA** Kelly and I had a great evening of food and hospitality at the Wolf Hotel in Saratoga. We had a thoughtful conversation with folks about the Wyoming Business Council, the University of Wyoming, and something I hear about all across the state: the growing lack of civility in politics. People are looking for leaders who can disagree without making each other enemies- something we have agreed to hold to in this race. A big thank you to Chuck and Laurie Box and Stu and Daney Tanner for bringing everyone together. Thanks to everyone who came out and spent the evening with us

subject: Bring wholesome messaging back to children's entertainment
body:
You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with “entertainment” that grooms children

| | | You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with "entertainment" that grooms children.
---
| |
---
| | Dear Friend in Faith,Please – for the sake of all our families – take it from me as someone who’s lived and worked in Hollywood my whole life... You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with “entertainment” that grooms children.You may remember shows with wholesome messages like Father Knows Best, Marcus Welby, M.D., and even Dennis the Menace.But today when children turn on the TV, they see a Drag Queen leading the Pride Parade on _Blue’s Clues_...

body:
Paxton’s strategy to win is undemocratic.
#
Peter,
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has spent years using the power of his office to target Latino civic power in Texas.
[](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260620-1.lLQqdN&amount=3&%3Brefcode=em20260620-277&t=1&akid=277%2E1366028%2E1w102X)
_**Now he’s the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate.**_
Which means the fight over Latino voter registration, turnout, and representation in Texas could decide Paxton’s political future and who will represent Texas in the U.S. Senate.
**[If you’re ready to help end Paxton’s political career and elect a leader who will fight for _all_ Texans and their democratic right to vote, rush in $3 today to power our voter registration and mobilization work in Texas through November.](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260620-1.lLQqdN&amount=3&refcode=em20260620-277&t=2&akid=277%2E1366028%2E1w102X)**
For years, Paxton has pushed baseless claims about voter fraud while going after Latino-led civic organizations, voter registration groups, and volunteers in the name of election integrity.
He’s even gone so far as to raid home offices and private residences — and **15 Latino Democratic officials and volunteers were indicted last year.**
His attacks have even left essential organizations that help voters participate in democracy struggling and volunteers intimidated. Now they’re running out of funds due to the unnecessary lawsuits brought on by Paxton.
And that’s exactly the strategy he means to use.
He knows Latino voters are a decisive force in Texas, and he knows that if he silences or discourages enough voters this November — he’ll win.
But we’re fighting back. There are more than 6 million Latinos eligible to vote in the state, and millions more still need to be registered, contacted, and mobilized before November.
[**So Peter, if you’re ready to help stop Ken Paxton, chip in $3 today to power our voter registration and turnout work in Texas.**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260620-1.lLQqdN&amount=3&%3Brefcode=em20260620-277&t=3&akid=277%2E1366028%2E1w102X)

Thank you,
Voto Latino

---
I want to clear up a few myths I keep hearing about the midterms — not just because they matter for turnout, but because this election is going to be about trust. In NEPA, corrupt politicians have broken our trust. We can’t act like that doesn’t affect how we move forward. _**Myth:** Because Democrats did well in 2025, November will take care of itself._ **Fact:** Momentum helps, but we have real work to do to rebuild people’s trust. Voters are tired of insiders who say one thing and do another. **Rob Bresnahan campaigned on banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks — then he traded hundreds of times while voting on bills that affect the companies he holds stock in.** He said he’d never cut Medicaid, then voted to kick thousands of our neighbors off it. We can’t accept that kind of behavior — we also can’t sit back and assume other voters will take care of it. _**Myth:** Corruption is just a Washington problem — it doesn’t touch our lives here._ **Fact:** Corruption shows up in local budgets, in who gets contracts, who gets jobs, and whether families can keep their health coverage. I saw this in Scranton when I first took office as mayor: when insiders divert resources, neighborhoods lose services, unqualified people hold critical positions, small businesses suffer, and families pay the price. Rob Bresnahan’s stock trades and votes haven’t been abstract — they’ve coincided with decisions that put coverage and opportunity at risk for our neighbors. _**Myth:** All politicians are the same, so there’s no point fighting it._ **Fact:** I ran for mayor of Scranton as an independent because that excuse was failing our city. Some people, like Rob Bresnahan, use public office to profit. Others use it to serve people: replacing street signs, fixing potholes, balancing budgets, and protecting healthcare. We can and _should_ insist on representatives who serve, not trade on their public office. _**Myth:** Small donations can’t combat the flood of Republican cash._ **Fact:** What counters big money is clarity and organization. We can’t outspend every attack, but we can make sure our message — that NEPA deserves honest representation — reaches voters early and often. **That starts with resources to run an honest campaign that shows up in communities, holds Rob Bresnahan accountable, and reminds voters what real public service looks like.** **I’m running because our government should work as hard as the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania, not for insiders or politicians' wallets.[Our race was just upgraded to a TOSS-UP and all roads to the House majority run through this district. name: Mark Guethle, IDCCA President
subject: Some thoughts about being re-elected
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Illinois Democratic County Chairs' Association
body:
Team,

I’m so honored today to have been re-elected as the President of IDCCA. I thought I could take some time this afternoon to talk to you about my experience in local politics, and why I’m so invested in IDCCA’s mission.

I started my career as a union organizer with Painters District Council 30, and assisting with labor organizing with the Illinois AFL-CIO. These were roles I proudly held, because I believe that working people are a critical base of the Democratic Party – and unions and labor are some of the levers of power that working people have to force change in our country.

I also wanted to get involved locally. That’s why I ran for Precinct Committeeperson and Village Trustee in my community. I believe that all politics is local and there is where I know I can make the most positive impact.

Here’s the truth, folks: County Chair is one of the hardest and most thankless jobs in the Democratic Party. My fellow Chairs and I aren’t doing it for power or glory. We do it because we believe in the power of our values, the impact that local organizing can have, and the good that the Democratic Party can do for our country.

In 2002 I made the decision to run for County Chair of the Kane County Democratic Party. When I started, Kane County wasn’t as blue as it is today. I had a vision of getting back to the basics of talking to voters and listening to their concerns. That is the vision that I shared with my fellow County Chairs and where I believe the IDCCA should focus our attention.

I’ve stayed involved with IDCCA for so long because I also believe that we can’t take our voters for granted, nor can we take our previous success for granted. We win, and continue to win, because we continue to put in the work to earn those victories.

IDCCA does the work to build our bench and build our Democratic infrastructure all across our state. Democrats win because of the work that we do down the ballot.

And with as important an election year as 2026 will be, we know that we can’t stop that work anytime soon. That’s why I care, and that’s why I keep up this work.

[**I’m so proud to be the President of the IDCCA, and I hope you’ll join me in supporting IDCCA’s critical mission with a contribution right now.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133705026/628784756/202828089?amount=25&refcode=IDCCA_EMAIL_210626_FR_Mark-Election&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDU1NzIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjdjZDViMTMtZWI2Yy1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNmQ2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=A1uhF7VKpPSpZy-8PyA6q2V-qnKnFpc6vHSZxUM15q4=)

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | On August 7th President Trump signed Executive Order #14330. We didn't write an op-ed about it. We didn't demand a hearing. We sent an undercover journalist with a hidden camera, and we got one of the company's own managers to admit, on tape, that the firm did roughly 20% of the work and passed the rest through to others. "Pass-throughs are a great thing," she said. We published it. The next day — **not the next year, the next day** — the Small Business Administration suspended ATI from federal contracting government-wide, along with three of its executives. The Treasury Department froze roughly $253 million in contracts pending investigation. The Treasury Secretary referred the matter to the Department of Justice. **One camera. Over the course of one evening, on hidden camera, he gave up protective formations, shift schedules, the Vice President's travel plans — even photos he had taken aboard Air Force Two. We published it. **Within hours** , the agent was placed on administrative leave, his security clearance suspended, his access to every agency system revoked. The footage is the argument. body:
We’ve been going through our supporter files ahead of the FEC deadline at the end of the month, and here’s what I noticed:
|

---
Hi Peter, it’s Maggie, Roy’s finance director.
We’ve been going through our supporter files ahead of the FEC deadline at the end of the month – and I noticed that **you haven’t made a donation to our campaign before.** Yet, even by opening this email, you’re one of Roy’s most engaged grassroots supporters – so today, we’re hoping you’ll take the next step and chip in.
Here’s why: We’re pacing behind our fundraising goals for June.
**That means we’re heading into one of the most important deadlines of the election – the quarterly FEC public fundraising deadline – a step behind where we should be.**
Coming up short would force us to scale back our TV ads, voter outreach efforts, volunteer recruitment and more – and it would send a public signal to the GOP that we won’t be able to fight back against the money they’re already dumping into this race (... nearly $100 million so far).
[**That’s why I’m reaching out, Peter, and it’s why I have to ask: Will you chip in $5 for the first time today to help us get back on track and ensure we have the critical resources we need to flip North Carolina’s Senate seat blue?**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/11942?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk691&amount=5&t=8&akid=1824%2E124072%2EL10Sft)

When I was a kid, reading this kind of headline would have been unimaginable: [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133709684/628794321/724725427?amounts=10,15,25,50,75,100,250&refcode=email_062026_pappas&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxY2NmMmEyMy0wMjZkLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LkrSSm8Ay3nmVDpZrk6s-8KYF4DrZnrRh41HT5ClLq4=) Growing up as a gay person in New Hampshire, I never imagined I could live out — let alone run for U.S. Senate. **But my community showed me what's possible.** You helped me win _four times_ in one of the most competitive congressional districts in the country. We’ve made tremendous progress since I was younger. But there’s still something we’ve never done. **We’ve never elected a gay man to the Senate.** To be clear, I’m not running for Senate just to make history. I’m in this race for the people of New Hampshire – **_all of us._** But the prospect of moving the needle of progress forward is deeply meaningful to me. This is an opportunity for representation in the Senate. It’s also important that LGBTQ+ people have more seats at the table at a time when our rights are coming under attack. **We can win this election for the people of New Hampshire, charting a path forward for our shared future – and we can tear down barriers and make history at the same time.** [Will you split a $25 contribution between my campaign and John Hickenlooper right now to stand with me in this historic fight?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133709685/628794322/724725427?amounts=10,15,25,50,75,100,250&refcode=email_062026_pappas&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxY2NmMmEyMy0wMjZkLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LkrSSm8Ay3nmVDpZrk6s-8KYF4DrZnrRh41HT5ClLq4=) **Thank you for supporting me in this campaign.** No matter who you are, who you love, who you pray to, or where you're from — know that I'll always have your back. With gratitude, Chris

subject: What does a Weekend of Action cost?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Francesca Hong
body:
We crunched the numbers
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260620-2939)
Peter,
You may have heard: We’re having a Weekend of Action today and Sunday ([sign up, there’s still time!](https://act.francescahong.com/go/13828?t=1&akid=2939%2E105371%2EWyNGCv)). Ever wonder how much these things cost?
We’re a people-powered team launching canvassers all over the state, from Rock County to Superior. But as the saying goes, nothing in life is free. Even though all of our door-knocking is volunteer led and driven, Team Hong needs literature, yard signs, sign-in materials, and buttons.
**Our top-notch accounting team crunched the numbers, and we think it costs (roughly) $100 per launch in materials!**
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260620.Cn8Owj&refcode=em20260620-2939&t=2&akid=2939%2E105371%2EWyNGCv)_Cute, yet so expensive..._
We’re asking you to help us keep up these awesome launches, and fund our door knocking across the state. We had 30 launches statewide this weekend, so **our** **goal is to raise $3,000 tonight** and keep our organizing going strong as we head towards August.
[Please chip in $10, $20, or more if you’re able to help us reach our goal.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260620.Cn8Owj&refcode=em20260620-2939&t=3&akid=2939%2E105371%2EWyNGCv)
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260620.Cn8Owj&refcode=em20260620-2939&t=4&akid=2939%2E105371%2EWyNGCv)
And if you’re nervous about your first time door knocking, we totally get it, but we gotta say -- everyone had a blast today, and we’d love to send you out with a buddy to learn sometime soon!
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260620.Cn8Owj&amount=5&refcode=em20260620-2939&t=7&akid=2939%2E105371%2EWyNGCv)**
With gratitude,
— Team Hong
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260620-2939&t=8&refcode2=2939_105371_WyNGCv&akid=2939%2E105371%2EWyNGCv)**
